title: The Crystal Payday

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: I watered this square so it would grow more crystals.
directions: [board: a White Muju stands on a square near home. Pip lowers a watering can over it. Nothing happens. A puddle spreads. Beside the square, an empty bucket and a laminated sign reading PAYDAY.]

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: It had four crystals. It has four crystals. Squares run out. They never fill up.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Then today we find out what four actually pays.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: From the drawer. Proposal: add a Mining button. Overruled. There is no Mining button.
directions: [card: PIP'S AMENDMENTS (PENDING). Click slides the drawer open and lifts out one card.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: This is the Muju. Its Mining number is three.
directions: [card: the Muju. Mining three.] [board: the Muju's square labelled RESERVE 4. Every other square dimmed.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: The square under it holds four crystals. That is the reserve: the crystals still sitting in the square.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Bucket three. Puddle four. Took three.
directions: [sfx: crystal clink] [board: your turn ends. Three crystals slide off the square into the bank. The square flips from 4 to 1.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: It took the smaller of those two numbers.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: I am standing professionally.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Moving or attacking does not stop payday. Collect from the square where you end.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Now it is your next turn end. Nobody has touched this square.
directions: [card: EVERY piece of yours collects at your turn end, even one that moved, attacked, was bought, or put on a new hat this turn.]
[board: same Muju, same square, now labelled RESERVE 1. Card beside it: the Muju, Mining three. Banner: YOUR NEXT TURN END. NOBODY ELSE TOUCHED THIS SQUARE.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: The Muju still has Mining three. The square has one crystal left.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: How many crystals does the Muju collect now?

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Three. Bigger number, bigger bucket.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: No rush on this one. Or just watch the bucket with me.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: One crystal, and room to spare in the bucket.
directions: [board: the Muju tips its bucket over the square. One crystal rattles in. The bucket is still mostly empty. The square flips from 1 to 0 and goes grey.] [sfx: crystal clink]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Three was the Muju's number. One was the square's number. Next payday here is an Empty Payday.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Bucket or puddle. You carry the smaller one.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: In rules words: a piece takes its Mining number, or whatever the square has left. Whichever is smaller.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: I tried telling it an encouraging story. Still empty.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Reserve: unchanged.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Turn one dial. This Radi has Mining zero.
directions: [card: EVIDENCE. Proves: this square, this piece, this turn end. Not checked: every other square, and what Black does next.]
[card: the Radi. Mining zero.] [board: a Radi standing on a square labelled RESERVE 16]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: The square under it is holding sixteen.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Bucket or puddle.

lines.speaker: CLICK
lines.text: Bucket. The bucket is zero. The Radi collects nothing.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: So my business needs crystals where the piece ends. The square it left pays nothing.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Whether it is still standing there next turn, I do not know yet.

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: The Standing Business is closing. The new one picks squares. I call it the chief financial bucket.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: New games use this Unequal routes map. Home squares hold eight crystals each. The brighter expansion squares hold sixteen each. Ordinary ground holds four, and the middle cluster holds eight. Empty squares are roads with no crystals. That makes five hundred four crystals altogether. Mining lowers a square's reserve. It never refills.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Every friendly piece collects at your turn end, including pieces bought or promoted that turn. Mining uses no actions. The bank is spendable money; total income remembers everything you collected, even after you spend it.

supplement.title: Every friendly piece gets payday
supplement.body:
Moved, attacked, bought or promoted: still collects.
Mining costs 0 actions.
Bank = crystals available to spend.
Total income = all crystals collected so far.

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Before you end a practice turn, say the payday out loud. Then watch what arrives.
directions: [card: SAY THE PAYDAY. THEN WATCH IT ARRIVE.]

lines.speaker: COACH
lines.text: Today was plenty if you want it to be. Next time the shop opens. What can our crystals buy?

question: How many crystals does the Muju collect now?
